concept: DriverBench task medians and equal-weight composite interpretation

claims.text: At specification revision 775c4bce1bfe1c409b947eae1f3eab6975fccfe3, a task score is its defined task size divided by the 50th-percentile iteration wall-clock time. The specification reports decimal MB/s (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes), whereas the C implementation README labels its output bytes_per_second. Convert units before comparing those outputs. (medium confidence)

In the pinned composite table, DriverBench = (ReadBench + WriteBench)/2, with each component an arithmetic average of its listed tasks. There are five read tasks and thirteen write tasks. Thus each read task has coefficient 1/10 and each write task 1/26 in DriverBench. These coefficients are derived from the table: equal weighting applies within each averaging stage, not across a flat list of all eighteen tasks. (low confidence)

The pinned specification times only each do-task phase with a high-resolution monotonic timer or the closest language equivalent. Setup, before-task, after-task and teardown are separate phases. Iterations contain many operations, so their median timing is a task-batch statistic; it is not a measured per-request latency percentile. (low confidence)

The pinned specification reports BSONBench, SingleBench, MultiBench and ParallelBench separately. SingleBench excludes Run Command. BSONBench is excluded from overall DriverBench because the other tasks already include encoding and decoding. The overall formula averages ReadBench and WriteBench, not the four task-complexity composites. (low confidence)

The specification defines DriverBench vX.Y: minor clarifications increment Y with little expected comparison impact; changes such as scoring weights, tested MongoDB version or hardware increment X because older scores are unlikely to be comparable. A reproducibility record should therefore pin the specification and implementation revisions, datasets, driver and runtime/compiler versions, warm-up policy, and server configuration. The record recommendation is an inference from this versioning rule and the specification’s explicit language-family and JIT differences. (low confidence)

DriverBench uses the task median for scoring and retains other timing quantiles for diagnostics. The iteration guidance combines a one-minute cumulative execution minimum with stopping after 100 iterations or five minutes, whichever is shorter; JIT implementations may discard warm-up iterations. Record actual iteration counts and warm-up policy when reproducing a result. (medium confidence)

The pinned changelog records added Client and Collection BulkWrite tasks on 2024-12-23, a DEEP_BSON data update on 2026-01-21, and a corrected DEEP_BSON score size on 2026-06-02. Consequently a benchmark name alone cannot establish identical task membership or score numerators across historical results; compare the actual revisions and dataset definitions. (low confidence)

The pinned specification sorts N iteration times ascending and selects index int(N*p/100)-1 for percentiles 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95, 98 and 99. Reproduction should preserve this literal formula rather than substitute a library percentile default: NIST documents several incompatible percentile estimators. For N=100 and p=50, the specified index is 49; averaging the two central observations changes the scoring procedure and can change the score when those times differ. This index example is a direct calculation. (medium confidence)

Commit a9096ad069e8af0f5973c9d0ca75da57e4c63616 removed specification-version front matter, including benchmarking Version 1.4. Consequently, preserve a source commit rather than inferring the benchmark generation from an absent version field. (low confidence)

DRIVERS-3486 tracks an AI-agent analysis awaiting investigation. It flags configuration TBDs, optional JIT warm-up, stopping-rule ambiguity and missing reference outputs; treat these as review allegations rather than established defects or an approved replacement procedure. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-22)

DRIVERS-3377 requires synchronizing deep_bson.json and changing DEEP_BSON task size to 22,840,000 bytes. It changes leaf names to leftValue/rightValue for strong-typed benchmarks; comparisons must identify the dataset generation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22)

Interpret the DriverBench arithmetic composite as the specified summary of task throughput scores. It does not establish an application workload speedup or a total-bytes/total-time rate. This is an interpretation of its formula; UCSD performance-analysis material independently shows that aggregation choice and implicit weighting can change benchmark conclusions. Inspect task results alongside the composite. (medium confidence)
